newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal car insurance to surge as EU boosts cover.
newsitem.headline: Portugal car insurance to surge as EU boosts cover.

text.p: Car insurance premiums in Portugal, which has the worst accident rate in Europe, are set to surge after a European Union law raised the minimum level of civil liability, brokers said on Wednesday.

Fernando Aleluia, a director with Lisbon broker Joao Mata, said a recent EU directive more than doubling the minimum civil liability required in third party car insurance to 120 million escudos ($777,000), would boost premiums in Portugal.
"People need more cover now, so premiums have gone up," he said. "People are also buying more cars in Portugal."
Jorge Henriques, managing director of Lisbon broker Sedgwick-Corretores de Seguros, said: "General insurance in Portugal is growing mainly because of car insurance."

Jose Sanches, a partner with Credite-Corretores de Seguros, said car insurance had good growth potential because premiums were among the lowest in the European Union despite the country's poor driving record.
He said claims had been higher than usual this year after one of the wettest winters this century.
Low car insurance premiums reflected Portugal's modest living standards within Europe, Sanches said. "Premiums should be proportionate to people's ability to pay," he said.
Motor vehicle insurance rose 10 percent year-on-year to 153 billion escudos ($992 million) in the first eight months of 1996, according to the Portuguese Association of Insurers (APS).
Another promising growth area was accident and sickness insurance as people relied less on the indebted public health system, insurance brokers said.
Much of the demand came from companies offering disability income protection to employees as an alternative to the overburdened social security system, Sanches said.
Accident and sickness insurance grew 9.3 percent year-on-year to 78.6 billion escudos ($509 million) in the first eight months of 1996, the APS said.
APS president Ruy de Carvalho said in an interview last month he expected accident and sickness premiums to grow by some 20 percent in Portugal this year, compared with 1995.
Increasing demand for sickness insurance resulted from disillusionment with long waiting periods and inadequate choice and facilities in state hospitals, he said.

Brokers said they expected insurance products to be sold mainly by retail and in-store banks in coming years, but they also saw good longer term prospects for telephone selling, now in its infancy in Portugal.

Portugal's two biggest retailers, Sonae Investimentos and Jeronimo Martins, have announced plans to open banks in their shopping centres in the coming months that will offer insurance and credit facilities.
"The big retailers will take advantage of the hundreds of thousands of people passing through shopping centres to sell them insurance," Sedgwick's Henriques said. ($1=154.2 escudos)
